files.document_title: Crossroads Pipeline Company LLC, Crossroads Expansion Project Non-Binding Open Season notice, February 9, 2026, page 2 map
files.what_it_shows: A regional schematic map. It shows the existing Crossroads line in red running from the Defiance, Ohio area west through LaPaz, Indiana to Schererville, Indiana, with arrows for gas moving from receipt points (Defiance, LaPaz, Cygnet, and the Shelbyville interconnect with the Rockies Express Pipeline) to delivery points (the ANR Joliet area, Schererville and the Northern Border North Hayden point). A long blue arrow runs west to northwest toward Iowa and South Dakota along the Northern Border Pipeline. It does not show where any new pipe would be built.

searched: The oilandgaswatch record for this project has no geometry and no attached documents.
Read the East Daley note and the sponsor open season notice on the Crossroads electronic bulletin board (via the PipeRiv copy of the notice).

FERC eLibrary full-text searches for Crossroads Pipeline, Crossroads Pipeline expansion project and Crossroads pre-filing in 2025 and 2026 found only routine tariff, annual blanket-activity and Form 567 filings; no application, prior notice or pre-filing request for this expansion.
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission annual blanket-activities report (docket CP26-315) was not opened.
notes: What the expansion physically is: according to the February 9, 2026 open season, it is up to 1.5 million dekatherms per day by as early as November 1, 2030, through looping of the existing system, extensions to new markets, added horsepower and capacity leases on ANR Pipeline and Northern Border Pipeline. East Daley describes the existing line as about 300 million cubic feet per day and just over 200 miles from northwest Ohio to the Indiana and Illinois border. The project is only at the non-binding open season stage, so no route, loop length or extension has been defined or filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The Northern Border deliveries reach Illinois to South Dakota through leased capacity, which is why oilandgaswatch lists IN, IL, IA and SD. The sheet has no length. A tracing of the existing Crossroads mainline (about 200 miles, Defiance to Schererville) would be an existing-pipe route, not the expansion. The URL checker returned a clean pass on the open season PDF. Recommend holding this row until a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission filing names the loop segments.
